metadata.title: Our team
metadata.description: Researchers, visiting colleagues, project students and alumni of the Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab.

intro: We bring together robotics, machine learning and bioengineering to study adaptive physical intelligence across scales. Meet the researchers and visiting colleagues, explore the 2026 project cohort, and discover the work of our alumni.

data.name: Dr Dandan Zhang
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.research: Adaptive physical intelligence for dexterous manipulation across scales
data.description: Dandan is an Assistant Professor at Imperial College London and founder of the Multi-Scale Embodied Intelligence Lab. Her research connects tactile sensing, robot learning, shared autonomy and optical and magnetic microrobotics. She joined Imperial in 2023 after a lectureship in Robotics at the University of Bristol, and received her PhD in Medical Robotics from Imperial in 2021.

data.name: Wen Fan
data.description: Wen develops vision-based tactile sensors and learning methods that connect robotic touch with physical understanding. His work combines sensor design, manufacturing and tactile perception for manipulation. He received an MSc from the University of Manchester in 2021, joined Bristol Robotics Laboratory as a research assistant in 2022, and subsequently moved his doctoral research to Imperial.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Learning object-centric physical properties from robotic touch for efficient perception and manipulation

data.name: Jialin Lin
data.description: Jialin studies magnetic microrobots, imaging and adaptation between simulation and experiments. His research connects microrobot perception and control with potential biomedical applications. He received an MSc in Robotics from the University of Bristol in 2022 and a BEng in Mechanical Engineering from Dalian University of Technology in 2021.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Adaptive sim-to-real algorithms for magnetic microrobots using ultrasound imaging

data.name: Lan Wei
data.description: Lan develops machine-learning methods for optical microrobot perception, including diffusion-based image generation and transfer between simulation and experiments. Her doctoral research also explores collaborative control. She received an ME in Computer Science from the University of Science and Technology of China in 2024 and a BE in Computer Science from Xiamen University in 2021.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Towards autonomous optical microrobots through perception, collaborative control and deployment

data.name: Zongcai Tan
data.description: Zongcai studies machine-learning methods for the design and control of optical microrobots. His doctoral project focuses on physics-informed control for biomedical research settings. He received an MRes in Medical Robotics and Image-Guided Intervention from Imperial in 2024 and a BE in Vehicle Engineering from Jilin University in 2022. His MRes project investigated human–robot shared control for optical manipulation with haptic guidance.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Physics-informed machine learning for optical microrobot control in biomedical applications

data.name: Kangyi Lu
data.description: Kangyi investigates physics-informed AI for autonomous microrobots and dexterous manipulation in lab-on-a-chip environments. She also contributes to project supervision on shared control for magnetic microrobot navigation. She received an ME in Electronic Information from Shanghai Jiao Tong University in 2024 and a BE in Automation from Nanjing University of Aeronautics and Astronautics in 2021.
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.project: Physics-informed AI for autonomous microrobots and dexterous micromanipulation in lab-on-a-chip systems

data.name: Piotr Blaszyk
data.affiliation: Department of Bioengineering · Imperial College London
data.research: AI for healthcare and surgical context awareness
data.project: Multimodal large language models for surgical context awareness
data.description: Piotr investigates how multimodal large language models can support surgical context awareness. His earlier MRes project explored sim-to-real transfer learning for robotic manipulation. He also supports research on uncertainty-aware surgical skill assessment.

data.name: Nitirak Rayabphand
data.description: Nitirak studies magnetic microscale robotics for medical applications at the University of Bristol. He received a master’s degree in Robotics Engineering from Osaka University in 2022 and a BE in Mechatronic Engineering from King Mongkut’s University of Technology Thonburi in 2015.
